annotations.title: Research a question over the corpus

description: Get a cited answer to a research question in one call, grounded in papers, books, patents, standards, Wikipedia and social sources (retrieval-augmented generation). Use for quick grounded answers; for thorough research, search and read sources yourself. Narrow with types, publication dates (issued_after, issued_before) or documents from search hits; each turn states its own. Pass conversation_id from a prior result to ask a follow-up in the same thread. Billed per turn: $0.03 plus $0.007 per requested document, $0.10 at the default limit of 10 and $0.24 at 30.

conversation_id.description: Continue a prior research thread; copy conversation_id from a previous result. Omit to start fresh. A follow-up does not inherit types, dates or documents; state them again.

documents.description: Answer about these documents only: copy hit.id from library search results (not web: ids). They are read whole and retrieval searches only them.

issued_after.description: Only results published at or after this Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC, inclusive); use this argument instead of after: in query. Any date bound excludes undated documents.

issued_before.description: Only results published at or before this Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC, inclusive); use this argument instead of before: in query. Must not be earlier than issued_after.

limit.description: How many supporting documents to retrieve into the answer context. Higher values cost more.

query.description: The research question in natural language. There is no two-word query or phrase limit. Preserve complete concepts and relationships; use full natural-language questions when useful. Quote established phrases whose wording must appear, including three-to-eight-word technical terms or longer known titles. Example: "long term exposure to air pollution" respiratory morbidity and mortality. Leave uncertain wording unquoted. For claim verification, search the relationship rather than requiring the entire statement verbatim. Every quoted span is required; multiple spans mean ALL, not alternatives. Matching uses ordered normalized indexed tokens, not byte-exact text; straight, curly, and guillemet quote pairs work. If results are sparse, relax optional phrases and explain the broader search; preserve wording the user explicitly requires. Quoted phrases remain required through query reformulation. Put dates and result types in their arguments, not in the question.

types.description: Result types the answer may draw on; omit for all. web: web pages (accounts that have paid); science: articles, proceedings, preprints, dissertations and reports; books: books and chapters; social: Reddit, Telegram and Discord posts.

name: machinelibrary_research

answer.description: Generated answer with inline [n] citation markers indexing into sources.

citations.description: One entry per inline marker in the answer.

snippet_index.description: Matched snippet within the source, when applicable.

conversation_id.description: Thread id; pass back as conversation_id to ask a follow-up in the same thread.

model_name.description: Model used to generate the answer.

sources.description: Documents the answer drew on, in citation order.

feedback_eligible.description: Whether this response supplies a feedback receipt covering this result. False for external web results or missing receipts (including citation backlinks). Omit false results from ratings and receipt-bound search_result context.

id.description: Returned document ID. Copy into feedback document_id only when feedback_eligible is true.

issued_at.description: Publication time, Unix seconds; null when unknown.

issued_at_datetime.description: issued_at as RFC 3339 UTC (2026-07-12T10:00:00Z); null when unknown.

snippet.description: Best query-matching excerpt, capped at 900 characters.

snippet_end_char.description: Exclusive Unicode scalar end offset in the full snippet_field; null when unknown.

snippet_start_char.description: Zero-based Unicode scalar offset in the original stored snippet_field (including content). Null means unknown, not zero.

snippet_table_header.description: When the excerpt continues a Markdown table, that table's caption, header and separator rows, which name its columns. Context only: not part of the excerpt or its offsets.

snippet_truncated_end.description: True: source text follows the excerpt. False: verified end of the field. Null: unknown (legacy or redacted source), NEVER equivalent to false.

snippet_truncated_start.description: True: source text precedes the excerpt. False: verified start of the field. Null: unknown (legacy or redacted source), NEVER equivalent to false. Whole sentences may be omitted; fetch context before resolving dangling references.

source.description: documents (papers, books, patents, standards, Wikipedia, YouTube transcripts), social (Reddit, Telegram, Discord) or web.

source_uri.description: Canonical URI to copy verbatim into fetch tools and citations. Null for records stored without any identifier: read them by passing search_result and cite them by title.

feedback_token.description: Receipt for feedback and attributing document reads. Copy only into search_result or the feedback tool; never include it in answers or citations.

title: Research a question over the corpus
